base_properties.human_readable: Gender Identity as Category Criterion (Identity-First Reading)

perspectives.label: Transgender Woman Denied Identity Recognition
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 1: TRANS WOMAN (SNARE) — Structurally mobile (could legally exit to male-identified status or choose institutional non-participation) but identity-locked: self-concept is constituted through woman/female identity. The constraint, in this reading, is that institutional barriers (bathrooms, documentation, legal recognition) prevent her from living her identity. She experiences the biological-sex reading as high suppression (cannot exit identity frame to avoid barriers) and extraction (forced into institutional spaces misaligned with identity). From her structural position, this is snare: the constraint uses institutional gatekeeping to force identity denial.

perspectives.label: Female-Bodied Individual in Identity-Aligned Space
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 2: CIS WOMAN (SNARE) — Considers herself a woman by both sex and identity. Under the gender-identity reading, her category membership is secure. However, she faces extraction when identity-inclusive definitions are applied to single-sex institutional spaces (refuges, sports, prisons) where her safety, dignity, or dignity-adjacent concerns may be affected by presence of trans women. The extraction is conditional and scope-dependent (medical contexts vs. sports vs. bathrooms have different risk profiles), but in spaces where her preferences are overridden by institutional identity-inclusive policy, she experiences this as extraction. Exit options are constrained (cannot easily exit institutions or change her identity/body to avoid the interaction).

perspectives.label: Identity-Inclusive Legal/Policy Institution
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 3: IDENTITY-INCLUSIVE INSTITUTION (TANGLED ROPE) — Enforces gender-identity-based category membership (e.g., legal recognition policies, trans healthcare access, anti-discrimination law). This institution benefits from the gender-identity reading: it has coherence, external legitimacy (aligns with medical/psychological consensus on gender identity as real), and reduces administrative burden (legal marker = self-declared identity). But it also requires active enforcement (must override sex-biology institutional barriers, resist sex-essentialist legal challenges, maintain policy coherence across contexts). The institution genuinely coordinates something (legal recognition, healthcare access, dignity protection for trans individuals) AND extracts (imposes costs on sex-essentialist institutions, overrides sex-based preferences in mixed-sex spaces). Genuine tangled rope: mixed coordination and extraction.

perspectives.label: Single-Sex Institutional Space Operator
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 4: SINGLE-SEX INSTITUTION (TANGLED ROPE) — A women's shelter, female prison, or women's sports league that must enforce admission criteria. Under the gender-identity reading, it must accept anyone identifying as woman, independent of biological sex. This institution faces high suppression (forced to override its operational criteria) and extraction (liability, resource strain, institutional mission drift if sex-based safety provisions are invalidated). But the institution also benefits from the coordination function: legal clarity that identity-based membership is legitimate reduces litigation risk (clearer policy = lower legal exposure) in some jurisdictions. The extraction is real (forced policy changes, resource costs, loss of sex-based institutional autonomy), but some coordination function exists (unified criterion across all institutional actors, clarity on admissions). Active enforcement is required (courts, regulators, advocacy organizations pressure institutions to accept the reading).

perspectives.label: LGBTQ+ Rights Organizations and Medical Consensus
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 5: ORGANIZED ADVOCATES (ROPE) — Advocacy organizations, professional medical bodies (APA, AMA, WHO), and gender clinics cohere around the gender-identity reading as a coordination standard. The coordination function is genuine: unified criterion for trans recognition reduces institutional fragmentation, enables trans individuals to navigate legal/medical systems coherently, and establishes legitimacy through alignment with expert consensus. These actors experience low suppression (medical guidelines support the reading; advocacy organizations advocate for it voluntarily) and low extraction relative to their power (they are not being forced into a disadvantageous framework—they are advocating for it). From their structural position, this is rope: pure coordination with minimal coercive overhead. Mobile exit options reflect that these actors can (in principle) shift to alternative framings; the fact that they do not signals genuine coordination rather than extraction.

perspectives.label: Bureaucratic Sex Category (Historical Residue)
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 6: BUREAUCRATIC SEX CATEGORY (PITON) — The institutional apparatus of sex classification (birth certificates, national IDs, administrative sex markers) persists as a vestigial category. The historical function was biological tracking (reproductive health administration, vital statistics). Under the gender-identity reading, this category becomes theatrical: the sex marker on a birth certificate no longer determines institutional access or rights (gender identity does), yet the apparatus persists due to inertia, legal path-dependency, and administrative convenience. Governments maintain sex categories on ID documents not because sex determines anything under the identity reading, but because the infrastructure exists and changing it is administratively costly. Theater ratio high (theater_ratio ≈ 0.65): the sex category remains visible but functionally obsolete. Extractiveness low (extractiveness ≤ 0.20): the piton causes minimal direct extraction; it is mostly a bureaucratic artifact.

perspectives.label: Gender Recognition Act / Self-Declaration Reform
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 7: GENDER RECOGNITION REFORM (SCAFFOLD) — Policies enabling legal self-declaration of gender (no medical gatekeeping, no diagnosis requirement, reversible process) are scaffold constraints: temporary coordination structures with sunset clauses built in. These reforms coordinate access to legal recognition (beneficial: trans individuals get identity-aligned documentation) with transparency/reversibility (sunset condition: if misuse reaches some threshold, the policy can be revised). The reform contains its own limitation: when evidence accumulates about misuse patterns (e.g., institutional fraud, bad-faith declarations), the scaffold can legitimately expire. Beneficiaries = trans individuals seeking rapid legal recognition. Theater low (the process is streamlined, not ritualistic). Extractiveness moderate (the reform imposes costs on sex-essentialist institutions but has articulated temporal limits, so it is not treated as permanent extraction). Sunset is explicit in many jurisdictions (e.g., Scotland's Gender Recognition Reform: 3-year review window).

perspectives.label: Analytical Observer (Identity as Irreducible Fact)
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 8: ANALYTICAL OBSERVER (MOUNTAIN CANDIDATE) — From a civilizational/universal perspective, this reading treats gender identity as an irreducible psychological/phenomenological fact: the subjective experience of gender is a direct datum of consciousness, comparable to the irreducibility of color qualia. The analytical observer risks seeing the category membership criterion (identity = category membership) as a natural law: identity JUST IS the relevant criterion at some level of analysis. However, the structural data contradicts this: the constraint has high suppression (0.62), requiring active enforcement against sex-essentialist institutions and counter-definitions. A genuine natural law would have suppression ≤ 0.05 and no identifiable beneficiaries. The beneficiary set (transgender individuals, identity-inclusive institutions) reveals that this is NOT a natural law but a constructed institutional criterion. The false summit detector will flag this perspective as naturalization.

omegas.question: Is gender identity a self-intimating psychological fact (phenomenologically direct) or a socially constructed category (dependent on institutional framing)?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Cross-cultural anthropological analysis of gender identity stability and institutional variation; neuroscience on the substrate of gender dysphoria; philosophical analysis of testimony and self-knowledge
omegas.impact: If phenomenologically direct: identity-based category membership is naturalizable (risk of false mountain). If socially constructed: category membership is contingent on institutional choice and deserves explicit normative justification (tangled rope/rope classification stands).
omegas.description: Ontological status of gender identity: direct psychological fact vs. socially constructed

omegas.question: Should gender-identity-based category membership be uniformly applied across ALL institutional contexts (bathrooms, sports, prisons, medicine, scholarship criteria) or context-variable (different contexts have different admission criteria)?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Empirical measurement of harm/benefit distribution across context types (bathrooms vs sports vs prisons vs medical vs social); normative analysis of which contexts warrant identity-only criteria vs. hybrid criteria
omegas.impact: If uniform: this reading's extractiveness and suppression are accurately captured at 0.58/0.62. If context-variable: this reading FORECLOSES or INFLUENCES the hybrid_contextual_reading, and the beneficiary/victim sets are incompletely specified (some contexts favor identity, others favor sex biology).
omegas.description: Whether identity-based category membership should apply uniformly across all contexts or vary by institutional context

omegas.question: What is the actual prevalence of transgender identity in the population, and how is it distributed across age cohorts, geographic regions, and institutional contexts?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Large-scale epidemiological surveys (>20,000 respondents) with consistent definitions; longitudinal data on gender identity persistence and change; institutional data on self-declared identity in settings where identity is privileged criterion
omegas.impact: Low prevalence + high geographic clustering: institutional impacts concentrate in certain regions/contexts; extraction profile is local/regional rather than national. High prevalence + uniform distribution: national scope extraction is accurate. High prevalence of identity fluidity or change: institutional scope of the identity-locked exit category is overstated.
omegas.description: Prevalence and distribution of transgender identity across population

omegas.question: Can institutional boundary enforcement (admission, recognition, documentation) be practically and reliably decoupled from biological sex criteria, or does some subset of institutional functions (particularly reproductive/medical functions) require sex-based information?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Operational analysis of institutional functions: medical record-keeping, reproductive health services, single-sex space provision, safety risk assessment; identification of contexts where sex data is material to institutional function vs. contexts where it is purely administrative
omegas.impact: If fully decoupled: identity-only criterion is operationally sustainable across all contexts; single-sex institutions can function while admitting trans women. If partially coupled: some institutional contexts REQUIRE sex-based information; this reading FORECLOSES hybrid_contextual reading's core premise in some domains, but not others.
omegas.description: Feasibility of institutional boundary enforcement decoupled from biological sex criteria

omegas.question: Is this reading's core claim about what the category MEANS (identity is the constitutive criterion) or about what CONSEQUENCES follow from that meaning (trans women are women)?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Textual analysis of advocacy statements, policy language, and judicial opinions framing the identity reading; logical analysis of whether the reading necessarily entails sex-based invisibility or could coexist with sex-tracking for specific purposes
omegas.impact: If primarily about meaning: this reading FORECLOSES sex_biology_reading within the same institutional framework (cannot hold both meanings simultaneously). If primarily about consequences: this reading COEXISTS_WITH or INFLUENCES sex_biology_reading—identity determines category membership for recognition purposes while sex information persists for other functions.
omegas.description: Whether this reading is about category meaning or institutional consequences

commentary.narrative_context: This constraint story instantiates ONE reading of a contested kernel: the meaning of 'woman' and 'female' as institutional categories. The identity-first reading holds that category membership is determined by internal self-identification with the gender category, independent of biological sex. Under this reading, a transgender woman (person born with male-typical reproductive anatomy who identifies as woman) is a woman for purposes of institutional access, legal recognition, social inclusion, and self-description. The constraint arises because this reading conflicts with alternative readings: the sex-biology reading (category membership determined by chromosomal sex, reproductive anatomy, and developmental biology) and the hybrid-contextual reading (category membership varies by institutional context—identity for social/legal purposes, sex for medical/sports/safety purposes). This story analyzes the gender-identity reading AS ONE LENS. It does not argue that this reading is correct, natural, or should be universal. It analyzes what structural consequences follow IF this reading is adopted as institutional policy. The core extractiveness (0.58) reflects that implementing identity-based category membership requires active suppression (0.62) of alternative framings and institutional autonomy, particularly in single-sex institutional spaces. The constraint also provides genuine coordination (medical consensus on gender identity, legal clarity, reduced fragmentation across jurisdictions), which is why it is classified as tangled_rope rather than pure snare—there is a real coordination function alongside real extraction.
key_agents: Transgender individuals (identity-seekers): Primary beneficiaries (organized/arbitrage) — gain legal recognition, institutional access, dignity affirmation. Beneficiary group: transgender_individuals_identity_seekers.

Cisgender women (female-bodied, identity-aligned): Conditional victims (moderate/constrained) — in some institutional contexts (single-sex spaces with safety/dignity concerns), experience override of sex-based preferences. Victim group: female_bodied_individuals_identity_aligned.

Sex-essentialist institutional actors: Organizational victims (institutional/constrained) — forced to redefine institutional criteria, lose sex-based institutional autonomy. Victim group: sex_essentialist_institutional_actors.

Single-sex institutional spaces: Infrastructure victims (institutional/constrained) — bathrooms, shelters, prisons, sports leagues that historically admitted on sex basis must now admit on identity basis. Victim group: single_sex_institutional_spaces.
Identity-inclusive legal/policy institutions: Institutional beneficiaries (institutional/arbitrage) — gain legitimacy, coherence, alignment with medical consensus. Enforce the identity reading.
Medical/psychological bodies (APA, AMA, WHO): Organized beneficiaries (organized/mobile) — gender identity reading aligns with professional consensus; voluntarily advocate for it.

Bureaucratic sex category apparatus: Vestigial institutional actor (institutional/arbitrage) — sex markers on birth certificates persist due to administrative inertia; become theatrical under identity reading.
commentary.logic_rationale: Extractiveness (0.58, rising from 0.25 to 0.58 over the measurement interval): Moderate-high. The identity reading requires institutional actors to override sex-based allocation criteria and institutional autonomy. Single-sex institutions (shelters, prisons, sports leagues, bathrooms) that historically admitted by biological sex must now admit by gender identity. This is extraction relative to institutional autonomy: sex-based institutional choice is suppressed. However, extractiveness is not maximal (0.72+) because the extraction is not maintained solely through external coercion—some institutional actors voluntarily adopt the reading (medical bodies, legal/policy institutions) because it provides coordination benefits. The measurement trajectory (0.25→0.42→0.58) reflects growing institutional implementation over time: as the reading becomes policy, extraction accumulates. Suppression (0.62, rising from 0.35 to 0.62): Moderate-high and increasing. Suppression is the forced override of institutional alternatives and sex-essentialist framing. Sex-essentialist definitions must be actively suppressed (legal redefinition, institutional policy enforcement, social stigma on dissent) for the identity reading to become institutional default. The measurement trajectory reflects institutional hardening: as the reading becomes settled policy, the suppression required to maintain it (resist alternative definitions, enforce institutional compliance) increases. This is not accidental—institutional settling of contested claims always requires increasing suppression of alternatives. Theater ratio (0.48, rising from 0.32 to 0.48): Moderate and rising. The identity reading requires less performative theater than sex-based classification (which has its own performative elements: genetic testing, anatomical inspection, chromosomal verification—equally arbitrary institutional rituals). The identity reading's theater comes from documentation processes (affidavits, legal applications, institutional attestations) that could be streamlined. The rise in theater reflects institutional standardization: as the reading becomes policy, documentation requirements increase (theater = ritual institutional validation of identity claims).
commentary.perspectival_gap: This constraint exhibits dramatic perspectival variation. The trans woman denied recognition sees snare (institutional barriers prevent identity expression). The cis woman in contested spaces sees snare (her preferences overridden). The identity-inclusive institution sees tangled_rope (genuine coordination + real extraction). The single-sex institution sees tangled_rope (forced policy change + some operational coherence benefit). The advocates see rope (voluntary coordination around shared standard). The piton perspective sees vestigial sex-based bureaucracy. The scaffold perspective sees temporary institutional arrangement with sunset. The analytical observer risks mountain (identity as natural fact) but structural data contradicts this. The perspectival gap reveals that category membership is not a natural fact but an institutional choice point. Different institutional actors experience the same structural phenomenon differently because they occupy different positions relative to the extraction/coordination flows. The gap between snare (victim perspective) and rope (advocate perspective) is the diagnostic signal: the victim experiences forced institutional change; the advocate experiences voluntary coordination. The gap reveals active enforcement is required (suppression = 0.62).
commentary.directionality_logic: Directionality (d) represents each agent's structural position relative to this specific constraint. Transgender individuals identifying as woman (beneficiary status + organized power + mobile exit options in some jurisdictions) derive d ≈ 0.25 → f(d) ≈ 0.02 (low effective extraction, institutional benefit). Sex-essentialist institutions (victim status + institutional power but constrained exit—cannot exit institutional space without ceasing to exist) derive d ≈ 0.75 → f(d) ≈ 1.08 (high effective extraction; suppression of institutional autonomy). Cisgender women in contested spaces (conditional victim, moderate power, constrained exit—can exit institutions but at cost of social/institutional participation) derive d ≈ 0.58 → f(d) ≈ 0.75 (moderate extraction, significant experienced harm). Identity-inclusive institutions (beneficiary status + institutional power + arbitrage exit) derive d ≈ 0.15 → f(d) ≈ -0.08 (negative effective extraction—institutional benefit and voluntary adoption). The directionality chain shows why beneficiaries voluntarily adopt this reading (institutional coherence, legitimacy, expert alignment) while victims experience it as forced institutional change (d values favor extraction toward institutional beneficiaries, away from sex-essentialist institutions and some cis women in contested spaces).
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: The mandatrophy (ambiguity between recognizing trans women as women and avoiding extraction from cis women / institutional autonomy override) is irreducible at the constraint level. It cannot be resolved by measuring extractiveness more carefully or finding the 'true' type. The mandatrophy IS the core question: Can institutional category membership be changed from sex-based to identity-based without the change itself becoming extractive institutional power? The tangled_rope classification preserves this ambiguity: there IS genuine coordination (legal clarity, medical alignment, institutional coherence), AND there IS real extraction (institutional autonomy override, cis women's preferences suppressed in some contexts, sex-essentialist institutional actors forced to comply). The mandatrophy is resolved by accepting that institutional category redefinition ALWAYS involves both coordination and extraction—there is no pure coordination in contested definitional change. The identity reading is not exceptional; it is exemplary of how institutional meanings change under political pressure. The classification stands as tangled_rope: both aspects are structural, both are real, neither dominates.
commentary.kernel_context: This constraint is the gender-identity reading of the contested kernel: woman/female category definition. The kernel is formalized (codified in law: birth certificate categories, legal recognition procedures, anti-discrimination protections) but its meaning is formally contested. Three readings compete: (1) GENDER-IDENTITY READING (this constraint): category membership = internal gender identification. (2) SEX-BIOLOGY READING (sibling constraint): category membership = chromosomal/reproductive/developmental sex. (3) HYBRID-CONTEXTUAL READING (sibling constraint): category membership varies by institutional context (identity for social/legal, sex for medical/sports/safety). This reading instantiates the gender-identity pole. The core premise is that the psychological/phenomenological fact of gender identity is the constitutive criterion for category membership. The sibling readings contest this premise. The reading_relations and axioms below document the structural relationships between this reading and its siblings.

network.dual_formulation_note: The woman/female category definition kernel decomposes into three structurally distinct constraint stories with different ε values. The identity reading (this constraint, ε=0.58) treats identity as constitutive. The sex-biology reading (ε≈0.40, tangled_rope/mountain) treats sex as natural law. The hybrid-contextual reading (ε≈0.45, scaffold/tangled_rope) treats context-variance as the legitimate institutional solution. These are not different measurements of the same constraint—they are different institutional choices with different extractiveness profiles. The network links document the causal upstream/downstream structure: the kernel (the contested meaning of 'woman') drives downstream constraints in institutional contexts (sports, single-sex spaces, legal recognition).
